facts.fact: Guatemala is home to the resplendent quetzal, a brilliantly colored bird so treasured that the country's currency is named after it and killing one was punishable by death in ancient Maya times.
facts.flagElement: the green bird silhouette in the upper left

facts.fact: Lake Atitlán is ringed by three towering volcanoes that rise directly from its shores, creating one of the world's most dramatic volcanic lake landscapes.
facts.flagElement: the three triangular peaks rising from the blue base

facts.fact: Guatemala produces some of the world's finest jade, and the ancient Maya valued green jade more highly than gold, using it for royal masks and ceremonial objects.
facts.flagElement: the jade green color dominating the upper portion of the flag

decoys.overlap: Famous for jade (greenstone/pounamu) and has a distinctive native bird culture (kiwi), but lacks the volcanic lake landscape
Has dramatic volcanoes rising from lakes and shares Central American geography, but lacks the jade heritage and quetzal association
Home to many spectacular bird species in its cloud forests and has emerald (green gemstone) mining, but lacks the iconic volcanic lakes
